ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: People's Republic of China Anti-Money Laundering Law (revised 2022, effective January 1, 2023); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information by Financial Institutions (PBOC Order [2024] No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration and the Measures for Information Disclosure of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (SAMR); Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622); Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); Hong Kong Companies (Amendment) Ordinance 2018 establishing the Significant Controllers Register; Guidelines on Compliance with Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Requirements issued by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Companies Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Mainland China acceptance: legalize by the Hong Kong SAR Government's Authentication and Legalization Service under the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR, then affix the seal of the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs Office in Hong Kong; do not chain Hague Apostille because the PRC is a Hague Apostille Convention member for Hong Kong only with specific procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Registry Certificate) of the Hong Kong parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR and subsequent verification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC in Hong Kong; alternatively use the Hong Kong Government's electronic Apostille service if the receiving Mainland authority accepts it under the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Hong Kong parent company authorizing incorporation of the Mainland WFOE and appointing the legal representative and Power of Attorney holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong parent company board of directors and Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Hong Kong notary public, then authentication by the High Court of Hong Kong SAR, then legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate in Hong Kong if required; for a Mainland WFOE filing, the simplified path is the Hong Kong Authentication and Legalization Service plus the PRC MOFA Hong Kong Commissioner's Office seal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Amended Memorandum and Articles) of the Hong Kong parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy by the Hong Kong Companies Registry, then authentication by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR and legalization by the PRC MOFA Hong Kong office; never combine with a separate consular legalization path as the two are mutually exclusive

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Hong Kong parent company's principal bank confirming account conduct and beneficial ownership details
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Hong Kong authorized institution or licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signing by authorized bank officer before a Hong Kong notary public, then authentication by the High Court of Hong Kong SAR and legalization by the PRC MOFA Hong Kong Commissioner's Office; for cross-border use in mainland China, documentary authentication follows the Hong Kong legalization route, not a general Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency of the Hong Kong parent company's directors and shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong licensed trust or company service provider (TCSP)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the TCSP's certification signature by a Hong Kong notary public, authentication by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR, and legalization by the PRC MOFA Hong Kong office; if the receiving mainland authority is a bank, it may accept the bank's own authentication protocol but must include the PRC-required legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The WFOE must conduct enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories by screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, PRC and Hong Kong sanctions lists, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's PEP database. Screening must include politically exposed persons (PEPs) defined as individuals entrusted with prominent public functions domestically or abroad, their family members, and close associates, with a look-back period of at least 12 months after leaving office for domestic PEPs and indefinite for foreign PEPs under the revised PRC AML Law. All hits require escalation to the AML compliance officer, risk-based enhanced due diligence, board-level approval, and suspicious transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit of the People's Bank of China, the Hong Kong Joint Financial Intelligence Unit, and, where applicable, the Customs and Excise Department. Negative news screening, sanctions ownership analysis at the 25% threshold, and ongoing transaction monitoring are mandatory and must be documented in a written AML/CFT risk assessment before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the local SAMR bureau online name pre-registration portal; for Hong Kong parent company name verification, the Hong Kong Companies Registry Cyber Search Centre and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must have a Chinese statutory name registered in simplified Chinese characters. The name must comply with the Provisions on Administration of Enterprise Name Registration, consisting of administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and company organization form. English names are optional but if used, must be transliterated consistently with the Chinese name and cannot be misleading. Phonetic transliteration is required when the foreign investor's name is in a non-Chinese script. The four-tier naming convention is: (i) administrative division; (ii) distinctive name selected by the applicant, which cannot be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name or a well-known trademark; (iii) industry or business scope description, which for this entity shall include 'pipeline finance', 'factoring', or 'supply chain management' subject to licensing; and (iv) company type, limited liability company or WFOE limited liability form. The name cannot contain foreign letters except as approved for the parent company's transliterated name, and cannot contain digits except as part of the specified industry code or trademark license. For the Hong Kong parent name, the Companies Registry allows English and/or Chinese names, but when filing in Mainland China the English name must be transliterated into simplified Chinese using standard Mandarin pinyin or the established Chinese name of the Hong Kong company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Group without a group company structure
City, county, district names that are not the actual registered address
Military, armed police, and public security terms
General manager as part of the name
Second-level administrative division abbreviations without SAMR authority
Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan as a standalone jurisdiction term without special approval
Foreign words or Chinese words implying foreign government patronage
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection notice stating the specific legal basis and prohibited grounds. The applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the immediate superior SAMR authority within 60 days of receipt, or within 30 days for Hong Kong Companies Registry name refusal before the Companies Tribunal or by judicial review in the Hong Kong Court of First Instance. The appeal must include the original application receipt, the rejection notice, a revised name proposal that cures the cited conflict, evidence of prior user rights such as registered trademarks or trade names, and a statutory explanation why the name is not confusingly similar. The SAMR authority must issue a written decision within 30 working days of the reconsideration filing; if no decision is issued within the statutory period, the applicant may treat the application as denied and bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court. For Hong Kong name objections, the applicant may also invoke the Companies Ordinance appeal mechanism and the court's inherent jurisdiction, and must simultaneously verify whether the objected name is protected as a registered trademark in Hong Kong or Mainland China to avoid infringement claims.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a Mainland WFOE engaged in accounts receivable factoring and cross-border reverse factoring. The Company Law of the PRC and the Measures for the Administration of Registered Addresses of Market Entities require a fixed and verifiable physical office address that is consistent with the actual place of business. The local SAMR office, the tax authority, and the licensed factoring regulator may conduct on-site verification before issuing the factoring license. Banks providing escrow and SWIFT wire facilities require a physical office inspection as part of KYC onboarding. A virtual office may be used only for secondary correspondence if the WFOE maintains a full-time operational office with identifiable staff, lease documents, utility bills, and physical files; otherwise it will trigger a registration abnormality and the business license may be revoked. In Hong Kong, a licensed TCSP may provide a registered office address, but that address cannot serve as the WFOE's substantive business address in Mainland China.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection by municipal SAMR, tax bureau, or local financial regulatory authority: (1) presence of full-time legal representative or senior manager on site; (2) authentic lease agreement with term exceeding one year; (3) utility bills and property management records matching names; (4) visible company nameplate; (5) on-site accounting records for the factoring ledger; (6) AML/CFT compliance manual with UBO register; (7) original business license and factoring license displayed; (8) employee contracts and social insurance registrations. Quantified risk: high, at 60% to 75% likelihood within the first nine months after incorporation, because the licensed factoring industry is under active municipal financial regulatory supervision and because the trade finance operation involves cross-border funds that trigger anti-money laundering inspections. The tax authority is likely to inspect within 12 months for invoices under the special VAT voucher system. The WFOE must be prepared for inspections with at least 72 hours of records available on-site and a designated inspection officer.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622, Laws of Hong Kong), sections 67-105 (incorporation by registration), sections 112-122 (articles of association, company name, registered office and certificate), sections 135-157 (share capital, directors, company secretary); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), sections 6-8; and, for the financing activity, the Money Lenders Ordinance (Cap. 163), sections 4-7; the PRC Foreign Investment Law (2020) if an onshore mainland WFOE subsidiary is subsequently formed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Companies Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 and Articles of Association of a local private company; issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law imposes no minimum issued or paid-up capital. The company may be incorporated with a share capital as low as one ordinary share, denominated in HKD or any other currency. No blocked escrow account or capital verification account is required by the Companies Registry. If an onshore mainland WFOE is later established as a subsidiary, the PRC Company Law also imposes no general paid-up capital minimum for a trade-supply-chain finance company unless a sector regulator prescribes otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THIS RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LIMITED (the "Company"), duly convened and held on [date] at the Company's registered office, records the unanimous resolutions of the newly constituted board. RESOLVED: ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTIONAL DOCUMENTS. The Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR and the Articles of Association of the Company are hereby approved, ratified and entered in the statutory records, and the subscribers named in the incorporation application are confirmed as the founding shareholders. RESOLVED: SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The share capital of the Company be divided into [number] ordinary shares at HK$[nominal amount] each, and the allotment of [number] ordinary shares to [Subscriber] at par, credited as fully paid in cash, is hereby authorized and approved. The Chairman and Company Secretary are authorized to execute the statement of capital, issue share certificates, and file all documents necessary to perfect such allotment. No issued share capital is required to be held in escrow under Hong Kong law, except where a counterparty agreement expressly requires a segregated settlement reserve. RESOLVED: REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be at [registered address], which is adopted for all statutory correspondence, service of process, and inspection of statutory records by the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department and other authorities. RESOLVED: BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall open segregated corporate settlement, collection and escrow accounts with one or more licensed banks, and the Director together with the Company Secretary, or any two designated Directors, shall be authorized to issue SWIFT MT101 and MT103 payment instructions, execute escrow mandates, sign trade-finance documentation, and approve all incoming and outgoing wire transfers relating to accounts receivable factoring and reverse-factoring operations. The bank is entitled to rely conclusively on such written instructions. RESOLVED: APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. [Name] is appointed as the first Director; [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary; and the Director and Company Secretary are jointly authorized to file Forms NNC1, ND1, ND2, annual returns, and all notices required by the Companies Ordinance and the Inland Revenue Ordinance. RESOLVED: GENERAL GOVERNING AUTHORIZATION. The Director and Company Secretary are authorized to negotiate, sign, seal and deliver all documents, agreements, powers of attorney, bank forms, regulatory filings and professional engagement letters necessary to carry into effect the trade-supply-chain factoring business of the Company and to retain solicitors, corporate-compliances officers, AML/CFT advisers and accountants for such purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Approval and Registry Pre-Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Public Registrar's e-Search and Name Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live name-precedence search on the Companies Registry's public e-Search portal using the exact proposed English name 'CN WFOE LIMITED' and any Chinese name. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Hong Kong company, and does not contain prohibited or undesirable words. Because the company will engage in trade finance, do not include words such as 'Bank', 'Deposit', 'Insurance' or 'Trust' unless the relevant regulatory licence is held. Obtain and record the name-check result, then reserve the name or include it directly in Form NNC1. This step is performed before incurring drafting and notarisation costs.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese company name
Identity document of the applicant or founding subscriber
Brief description of the intended trade factoring business
Companies Registry public search result or name-check record
Hong Kong correspondence address of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried by the Registrar, submit a revised name application with an alternative name and an explanatory letter demonstrating distinguishability from existing registrations. If the rejection is based on prohibited statutory words, remove such words and resubmit. The Companies Registry does not operate a formal appeal for name refusal, but a fresh application may be made at any time after the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation by Submission of Form NNC1 and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - e-Registry or Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory incorporation form, being Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation of a Local Company), and execute the Articles of Association in English. State the principal business code as ISIC 6492/NAICS 522298 and provide the details of the first director and company secretary. Sign the subscription statement and the statement of capital; declare the registered office address. File the full package electronically through the e-Registry or deliver it in paper form to the Companies Registry counter. Pay the statutory incorporation fee, and upon verification the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. After incorporation, the company must immediately proceed to business registration.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NNC1 signed by each subscriber
Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Statement of capital and initial shareholding details
Consent to act as first director
Consent to act as company secretary
Valid passport or Hong Kong identity card of the proposed director and secretary
Proof of registered office address
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues an objection or deficiency letter, cure the stated defect within 14 days by refiling the corrected Form NNC1, amending the Articles of Association or supplying a certified translation or identity proof. If the registrar refuses registration, make written representations accompanied by all curative documents; if the refusal persists, apply for registration under a corrected constitutional package or seek judicial review in the Court of First Instance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Inland Revenue File Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, apply to the Business Registration Office for a Business Registration Certificate using the prescribed IRBR form. The application must set out the registered office address and describe the principal activity as accounts receivable factoring, cross-border reverse factoring and trade-supply-chain finance. Attach the Certificate of Incorporation, the UEN notification and proof of address. Upon payment of the business registration fee and the levy, Inland Revenue issues the Business Registration Certificate. This certificate must be displayed at the registered office and renewed annually according to the Business Registration Ordinance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by Companies Registry
Completed IRBR business registration application form
Proof of registered office address (tenancy agreement or utility bill)
Description of principal business activity
Unique Entity Number notification from Companies Registry
Identity details of the sole director or controlling shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration application is suspended for missing information or an unverified address, respond by filing the missing declarations and a current tenancy or ownership document. Pay the overdue business registration fee plus any late fee if the one-month deadline is missed. A business registration certificate can also be retrieved online if the only issue is payment failure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution of the Board, Statutory Records and Bank/Escrow Mandate Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office of the Company; licensed bank account-opening desk; Companies Registry post-incorporation filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation and business registration, convene the first board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions. Approve the pro-forma first board resolution containing the registered office adoption, director and company secretary appointments, share allotment and bank signatory mandate. Open corporate bank and escrow accounts with a licensed bank by delivering the constitutional documents, tax file number if applicable, beneficial owner declarations and sanctions/PEP screening forms. Thereafter file any post-incorporation changes with the Companies Registry and maintain the statutory registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Duly executed first board resolution
Articles of Association and statement of capital
Bank account opening application and corporate mandate form
Register of Directors and Register of Shareholders
Share certificates and register of members
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declarations for KYC/AML purposes
Resumes or professional references of the appointed director and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account or requests additional information, promptly provide the enhanced due diligence package, including a certified board resolution, updated beneficial-ownership register and a detailed operating model for the factored receivables and escrow accounts. If the Companies Registry rejects any post-incorporation change form, correct the form and refile within 14 days; no prejudice arises if the filing is perfected before the offence notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factoring Business Licensing and AML/CFT Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Money Lenders Licensing Office, Companies Registry; Hong Kong Monetary Authority if restricted-deposit-taking licence is adopted; Inland Revenue for operating record
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the exact product design to determine whether reverse-factoring advances constitute licensed money lending under the Money Lenders Ordinance (Cap. 163). If the company will advance funds to suppliers in exchange for rights to receivables, make a full Money Lender's Licence application. The application must include the business plan, AML/CFT compliance manual, sanctions screening procedure, customer due diligence procedures, solvency evidence, and responsible officer declarations. If the transaction is structured as a pure purchase of receivables with no loan exposure, prepare a written legal opinion confirming exemption and retain the file for regulatory inspection. Implement a mandatory AML/CFT programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615).
required_dossiers: Money Lender's Licence application form (where applicable)
Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate and Articles of Association
Detailed business plan for trade receivables factoring and reverse factoring
AML/CFT policy manual, customer due diligence and sanctions screening procedures
Audited financial statements or bank references of the ultimate shareholder
List of directors, key officers and responsible person(s)
Independent legal opinion on the application of Cap. 163 and Cap. 615 to the proposed factoring arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Money Lenders Licence application is queried or refused, submit a comprehensive written response addressing the licensing officer's stated objections, including revised AML procedures and a clean corporate structure chart. If still refused, lodge a formal appeal under the Money Lenders Ordinance or seek judicial review. In the interim, cease any loan-like activity and limit operations to unadvanced invoice discounting supported by an independent legal opinion.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registry of Money Lenders, Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR; Hong Kong Monetary Authority for any deposit-taking or restricted banking product; no industrial licensing board is triggered because ISIC 6492 is a financial services activity with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Money Lender's Licence under the Money Lenders Ordinance (Cap. 163) for reverse-factoring credit advances; for true invoice discounting without loan elements, the company relies on its Business Registration Certificate and a documented exemption opinion, as Hong Kong does not maintain a separate 'factoring licence'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499). The registered operation is office-based trade finance and requires no EIA because no Schedule 2 designated project, manufacturing plant, chemical facility or warehousing site is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial point-source discharge. Office sanitary effluent must be disposed of through the municipal sewer in accordance with the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358); no VOC emission threshold is triggered; no hazardous waste is generated. Any electronic or office waste must be removed by a licensed collector under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure financial services; no Fire Services Department industrial permit is required. However, the leased office must hold a valid Fire Service Certificate (FS 251) and, if a material change of use is involved, a Letter of Compliance under the Fire Safety (Buildings) Ordinance (Cap. 572). No structural load inspection is needed because no racking or heavy warehousing equipment will be installed. As an employer, the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509), maintain emergency evacuation plans and obtain any labour registration required for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: National E-Tax Bureau (etax.chinatax.gov.cn), operated through provincial STA branches; export customs filings are handled through the China Single Window portal administered by the General Administration of Customs of China (GACC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The China WFOE is formed under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). After the SAMR issues the business license, the WFOE automatically receives the statutory Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the Tax Identification Number for enterprise income tax, VAT, and local surtaxes. The WFOE must complete tax registration through the E-Tax Bureau within 30 days of the license date, providing the articles of association, legal representative identification, financial accounting system document, registered address proof, and business license. The STA then activates the taxpayer file, determines Small-scale or General VAT taxpayer status, and enrolls the entity for monthly or quarterly VAT and annual corporate income tax filings. For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no Chinese establishment but with Chinese-source income, no USCC is required; the payer or the non-resident may apply for a non-resident taxpayer registration with the STA for withholding and treaty-claim purposes, using the home jurisdiction TIN. For the WFOE, the Chinese entity is the taxpayer and no separate offshore registration is needed for its local tax identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not permit a check-the-box or pass-through election for a WFOE; the WFOE is mandatorily a Chinese resident enterprise subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch election is available. The only elections are administrative: a business below the RMB 5,000,000 VAT general-taxpayer threshold may choose to become a general VAT taxpayer, and eligible taxpayers may elect to apply tax treaty benefits under the PRC/Hong Kong SAR double taxation arrangement, but neither changes the default entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (PRC VAT), administered under the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax and its implementing rules, and under the Value-Added Tax Law of the PRC effective 1 January 2026. The applicable rate for the WFOE's factoring and trade-finance services is 6%; the general goods supply rate is 13%, and the cross-border goods export rate is 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All VAT-taxable enterprises must complete tax registration; annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 trigger mandatory registration/classification as a General VAT taxpayer. Below RMB 5,000,000, the WFOE may be a Small-scale VAT taxpayer subject to simplified collection unless it voluntarily elects general status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Phase IV electronic invoice administration framework and the STA all-digital electronic invoice platform. VAT invoices (Fapiao) for factoring fees, including Special VAT Invoices, must be issued through STA-approved invoicing systems or system-to-system API interfaces connected to the E-Tax Bureau. Each invoice receives a unique tax-control number and digital anti-counterfeiting signature at issuance; invoice data, VAT returns, and customs declarations are reconciled in near-real-time by the STA. There is no foreign-style physical fiscal stamp; anti-fraud clearance is performed digitally by the national VAT invoice identification and verification platform, and every issuance, red-letter reversal, and void is reported immediately to the tax authority.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A General VAT taxpayer may apply the 0% VAT rate to exported goods when the goods physically leave China Customs territory, the taxpayer is the actual exporter/seller, the VAT invoice, customs declaration, logistics documents, and bank receipt are mutually consistent, and the foreign currency export proceeds are collected from the overseas buyer. Zero-rating of services is available only for categories expressly listed in the STA cross-border taxable services zero-rating and refund catalogue; factoring services supplied to non-residents are not zero-rated and may qualify only for VAT exemption if the service is wholly used outside China. Accordingly, the WFOE must separate the underlying goods export trade from the factoring commission and finance charges: the goods export is substantively zero-rated, while the factoring income is generally taxable at 6% unless an independent cross-border service exemption applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration for Goods (Customs Export Declaration Form / Bill of Entry) generated in the China Single Window
Bill of Lading (ocean full set), Air Waybill, or international railway/road consignment note evidencing physical departure from China
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the underlying export sales contract or purchase order
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Export Proceeds Collection Confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign exchange from the overseas buyer
SAFE and bank foreign exchange receipts/payments records and settlement records matching the customs declaration value
Export VAT refund application data transmitted through the E-Tax Bureau and cross-referenced to the customs declaration and proceeds receipt

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under China's foreign exchange administration framework, RMB is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including payments for goods, services, and remittance of lawfully declared dividends. However, the capital account remains regulated, and all cross-border capital movements require prior SAFE registration or approval. A WFOE establishes an FDI capital account; injected equity funds must be registered with SAFE through a designated domestic bank, converted in compliance with the foreign-invested enterprise capital settlement policy (positive/negative list approach), and may not be diverted into securities or entrusted loans unless specifically permitted. The repatriation of profits is permitted, but is conditioned on mandatory tax clearance, audited financial statements, tax withholding on dividends, and documentary proof that the profits arose from genuine business operations. In practice, banks require the annual audit, preferential tax or standard 10% withholding forms, and a formal board resolution before effecting outward remittance. Export receipts require receipt within statutory timeframes and are subject to the genuine-invoice verification system, although the mandatory surrender ratio has been zero since 2012; exporters may hold or convert proceeds subject to bank monitoring and trade data matching. For a foreign-invested factoring/licensing entity, each cross-border transfer must also be mapped to an approved SAFE business code, making the pre-transaction documentary compliance a make-or-break requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished mandatory export surrender. Receipts from exports must be collected within 90 days after the date of export declaration, unless a longer grace period is approved; the full amount must be brought into a domestic account and reported through the bank under SAFE's trade monitoring system. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted into RMB at the market rate, but any cross-border transfer must be matched to the customs declaration and invoice data to satisfy the 'three-way reconciliation' (goods, funds, declarations). Failure to collect within the statutory window triggers an exceptional reporting and penalty regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI settlement) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI settlement) and RMB Basic Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Operations Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut Business) are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in the PRC and are legally prohibited from maintaining RMB current accounts or foreign-exchange dominions for a WFOE. Under the Administrative Measures for the Payment Services of Non-Bank Institutions, non-bank entities cannot engage in cross-border renminbi settlement as a settlement bank in the sense of conducting KYC, foreign exchange verification, and SAFE reporting autonomously. Consequently, their viability for this structure is effectively zero. They may only function as a low-value collection gateway for e-commerce, not as the primary clearing infrastructure for factoring or trade settlement. Any use of such EMIs as an operational account would trigger a systemic AML breach and could lead to account freeze, licence revocation, and exclusion from the SAFE registry. The only compliant route is a domestic commercial bank account alongside licensed cross-border payment institutions that partner with banks and perform filings under SAFE supervision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE engaging in regulated factoring, the People's Bank of China's Beneficial Ownership Identification and KYC guidelines require the legal representative, at least one ultimate beneficial owner if a significant shareholder, and the designated authorised signatory to appear in person at the bank's physical branch for an interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted; some banks allow a notarised and apostilled power of attorney executed at the Chinese embassy or a Hong Kong notary public if the legal representative is abroad, but the mandatory biometric-phase and business-true-nature interview continues to require the operator or a fully documented proxy with a sealed power of attorney and the corporate chop to be produced at the branch. Given the medium-risk-enhancement designation, the prudent compliance position is to require physical attendance of the legal representative and the CFO/treasurer at the account-opening meeting, at a branch that has licensed trade and FX capabilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership of a Hong Kong parent company interdisted; ultimate natural-person shareholders are not visible from the initial incorporation documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cascaded corporate registry: HK Companies Registry certificates of incorporation, annual return (NAR1), register of directors and register of charges; Certificate of Incumbency issued by the registered agent; notarized stock transfer or subscriber forms; audited ownership chain to each UBO holding 25% or more; identity documents (passport, residence permit) of UBOs; a signed beneficial ownership institutional tier disclosure and AML sources-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring licence and regulatory approval are not evidenced, exposing the bank to the risk of facilitating illegal deposit-taking or unlicensed financial business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The WFOE must present the business license with receivables factoring scope, the local financial supervision bureau's administrative permission, evidence of the pilot scheme registration, the factoring management system and AML compliance programme, plus the commercial factoring business registration under the central bank's credit system where applicable. Also certification of no cross-business violation with deposit-taking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering through reverse factoring; underlying receivables may be fabricated with no movement of goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade package per invoice: copy of export customs declaration, logistics waybills (bill of lading, air waybill, courier tracking), purchase orders, VAT invoices, receivable assignment agreement, debtor notification receipts, and factory production evidence such as warehouse receipts and inspection records. For recurring flows, provide a borrower-side audit and an independent collateral verification report from a licensed accounting or probity firm, supported by the SAFE trade data matching record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons exposure embedded in cross-border counterparties; payment chain may involve sanctioned jurisdictions through Hong Kong routing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: At the entity level, provide a sworn list of all directors, shareholders, controllers, and counterparties from a recognised KYC database; sanctions screening reports against UN, EU, OFAC, and China's sanctions lists for both the platform and its clients; a PEP identification questionnaire with source of wealth documentation for any PEP-flagged individual; and an external corporate investigative due diligence report for any risk hit, prepared by a licensed compliance consulting firm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE should first complete FDI registration with the local Market Supervision Administration and obtain the SAFE Foreign Investment Registration through a designated bank. Inbound equity wires are settled as capital injection for equity subscription, using the relevant SAFE business code for FDI. The funds enter the USD/CNY capital account and must be converted under the capital settlement payment policy; each conversion is tied to a bona fide transaction such as rent, salaries, procurement, or licensed business expenses. A capital verification report by a Chinese-certified public accountant is required after the injection, and the bank must receive the proof of use (e.g., payment orders, contracts, invoices) within the regulatory monitoring period. Use of capital for securities, entrusted loans, or non-operating investments is prohibited except under specifically approved pilot schemes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic RMB disbursements to suppliers, use CNAPS/IPS clearing with reference to the underlying trade documents. For cross-border payments, SWIFT MT103 is the default direct settlement rail; commercial letters of credit are recommended for high-value import transactions where bank payment undertakings and document checking are required; documentary collections are acceptable when the WFOE has an established trade relationship. Every outward remittance must be supported by the invoice, contract, customs declaration where applicable, and a SAFE payment purpose code. Payments related to factoring must also reference the receivables assignment notice, the debtor payment undertaking, and the credit facility agreement to satisfy the underlying real transaction test. All foreign-exchange transactions are priced at the market rate and reported under the bank's head-office SAFE gateway.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts (delivery forwards) executed with a domestic designated bank, restricted to real trade exposure evidenced by export/import contracts and invoices; settlement occurs against the daily central parity rate on the value date.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps with commercial banks for hedging the principal and interest cash flows of SAFE-registered foreign-currency borrowings; the underlying debt must be properly registered and the hedging notional cannot exceed the outstanding exposure.
Client option products may be used to hedge firm committed foreign-currency receivables or payables, but naked options, leveraged FX derivatives, and speculative anticipatory hedging are prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore WFOE entities; any offshore NDF or quanto hedging arrangement violates the real-demand principle and is subject to regulatory enforcement, so only onshore deliverable instruments should be used.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days of the anniversary of incorporation date for each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate by delay: HK$870 (US$111.54) for up to 3 months, HK$1,740 (US$223.08) for 3 to 6 months, HK$2,610 (US$334.62) for 6 to 9 months, HK$3,480 (US$446.15) for 9 to 12 months; continued default beyond 12 months triggers administrative strike-off of the company and prosecution of directors under the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days before expiry of the current one-year business registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of HK$300 (US$38.46) per certificate; overdue business registration subjects the company to prosecution, additional penalties, and after three years of non-compliance the company may be struck off and the director held personally liable for the unpaid fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) together with Audited Financial Statements and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issuance of the return; standard issue date is 1 April for each fiscal year, and extended filing may be granted to 2/3 months when a tax representative is appointed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalties range from HK$5,000 to HK$50,000; understated tax liability may incur additional assessment of up to 10% of the tax undercharged; repeated defaults lead to the issue of estimated assessments and legal prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (BIR56A) and Individual Employee Returns (BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the end of the tax year (i.e., on or before 1 May) for the year of assessment ending 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an Employer's Return without reasonable excuse is punishable by a fine of HK$10,000 (US$1,282); the IRD may also issue a notice of increased penalty or initiate prosecution if the return is not filed even after reminder.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Money Lender's License Renewal (for trade finance and factoring activities under target scope)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Money Lenders Licensing Office, Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be lodged no later than 2 months before the expiry of the current 12-month money lender's license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on money lending business without a valid license is an offence under the Money Lenders Ordinance, punishable by a fine of HK$100,000 (US$12,821) and imprisonment for up to 2 years upon conviction; the company may also be struck off and all interest on outstanding loans becomes irrecoverable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full statutory audit by a licensed Certified Public Accountant is mandatory for (i) any Hong Kong company that does not qualify as a small private company or a member of a small private group, where small private status is satisfied when at least two of the three criteria are met in a financial year: total revenue does not exceed HK$25,000,000 (approx. US$3,205,128), total assets do not exceed HK$50,000,000 (approx. US$6,410,256), and the number of employees does not exceed 100; group figures are aggregated for group members. (ii) All licensed money lenders, factoring, trade finance, and payment entities are excluded from audit exemption because regulatory license conditions and the enhanced AML/CTF risk classification require independent CPA certification of financial statements regardless of size. (iii) The audit exemption is also unavailable to public companies, banks, insurance carriers, securities intermediaries, and any entity whose shareholders' resolution or articles require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), fully convergent with IFRS; eligible private companies may choose HKFRS for Private Entities instead, but licensed factoring entities in the medium-risk enhanced AML category are expected to apply full HKFRS due to regulatory disclosure expectations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a standalone annual UBO filing. The company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) under Part 17 of the Companies Ordinance, identifying all individuals and legal entities with significant control. The SCR must be updated within 15 days of any change in significant control information once the company becomes aware of the change. For shareholding transfers and issue of new shares, the Register of Members must be updated immediately, and a Return of Allotment (NAR6) must be lodged with the Companies Registry within 30 days of any allotment. The annual return (NAR1) must include a declaration confirming that the company has kept a compliant Significant Controllers Register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$500 - US$2,500 per annum for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 - US$12,000 per annum depending on transaction volume, cross-border factoring complexity, and number of bank custodians

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The statutory headline CIT rate is 25%. Preferential regimes available to a qualifying WFOE include: (i) a 15% reduced rate for certified High and New Technology Enterprises; (ii) a 20% rate with a 25% taxable-income reduction for Small Low-Profit Enterprises, producing an effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million subject to headcount and asset tests; (iii) a 15% rate for encouraged industries under Western Region development policy if the factoring and trade-finance activities qualify in a designated western region; (iv) a 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses, effectively a 200% deduction before the current sunset extension; and (v) no general mainland free-zone patent box for factoring income, although free trade zones may provide customs and foreign-exchange facilitation rather than CIT holidays. Any reduced rate must satisfy economic substance and eligibility record-keeping requirements; a factoring entity cannot claim preferential income without genuine operating activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (A-Class) together with supporting schedules including Form A105000 (Tax Adjustment Items), Form A105050 (R&D and staff expense adjustments), Form A107012 (Additional R&D Deduction), Form A108010 (Foreign Tax Credit), and the Related Party Transaction Reporting Forms. The filing is made electronically through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax portal (e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau) before the competent tax authority where the WFOE is registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional enterprise income tax returns must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The final annual return and settlement payment must be filed within 5 months after the end of the tax year (i.e., by 31 May for a 31 December year-end). If the WFOE adopts a non-calendar fiscal year, the 5-month period is measured from that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1 - Business Revenue and Turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate invoice turnover and operating revenue from accounts receivable factoring, reverse factoring commitment fees, discount interest embedded in receivables purchases, collection and trade-document processing fees, guarantee fee reimbursements, and foreign-exchange spread income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a resident enterprise for PRC tax, so its worldwide income is taxable and must be reported on an accrual basis. Cross-border factoring income derived from receivables arising from Chinese import/export transactions remains China-source income and must be declared; do not treat fees paid by foreign sellers or buyers as offshore income merely because the debtor is outside China. Fees or commissions received from the Hong Kong parent for client introduction or service arrangements must be reclassified as service income if the substance tests require, and transfer-pricing adjustments may allocate additional profit to the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 - Operating Costs, Expenses, and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of acquiring receivables, credit insurance premiums, legal and collection costs, personnel costs, commissions, office rent, depreciation, and other directly attributable factoring operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only reasonable, substantiated, and arm's length expenses are deductible. Payments to the Hong Kong parent for back-office, guarantee, or platform services must pass a benefit test and an arm's length analysis; duplicative or purely passive service fees are disallowed. Non-deductible fines, administrative penalties, and excess entertainment or gift expenditures must be added back later in the return. Any cross-border fee paid to a non-resident service provider must be supported by contracts, invoices, and proof of actual service performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 - Financial Expenses and Interest / Factoring Discount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on borrowings used in the factoring business, funding costs, guarantee fees, standby letter-of-credit fees, and any discount paid on transfer of invoices to co-funders or the Hong Kong parent financier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Characterize all amounts paid to non-resident funders carefully. If there is lending substance, the fee is interest for PRC withholding tax purposes. If the Hong Kong parent funds the WFOE with shareholder loans, the thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ratio is 2:1 for a non-financial enterprise; excess interest is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend, triggering outbound withholding tax. Withholding tax at the statutory 10% rate, or at the 7% China-HK DTA rate for qualifying interest, must be withheld from gross cross-border interest payments unless treaty relief has been substantiated. Factoring fees and discounts must not be artificially split to reduce withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Schedule A105000 and Related Party Transaction Disclosure Forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments reconciling accounting profit to taxable income, including add-back of non-deductible items, tax-exempt income, loss adjustments, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form A105000 and the Related Party Transaction Information Forms. Disclose all transactions with the Hong Kong parent: equity contributions, loan balances and interest, guarantee fees, management fees, IT or platform fees, royalty licenses, and receivables purchase or sale transactions. Prepare a contemporaneous Local File if the statutory thresholds are met and provide an arm's length benchmark, preferably CUP or TNMM for factoring services. If contemporaneous documentation is missing, the tax authority may apply an inverse burden of proof, adjust income, and impose separate documentation penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Loss Carryforward and Taxable Income Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of allowable tax losses brought forward against current taxable income under the statutory 5-year carryforward rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE's tax losses cannot be surrendered to or deducted by the Hong Kong shareholder; no group relief exists between mainland China and Hong Kong for CIT purposes. If the WFOE undergoes an ownership or core-business restructuring lacking commercial purpose, carried-forward losses may be invalidated under the business-continuity and control-continuity anti-abuse rules. The taxpayer must document continuity of the factoring business, preserve audited financial statements, and maintain loss schedules for at least 10 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Final Tax Payable, Preferential Rate Application, and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax computed at 25% or the applicable preferential rate, reduced by quarterly prepayments and any foreign tax credit, resulting in the net tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% general rate; use 15% for a certified High and New Technology Enterprise, or the effective 5% rate for a qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprise, only if all eligibility conditions are documented. After computing CIT, separately determine withholding tax obligations as agent for the Hong Kong shareholder: any declared dividend, interest, or royalty remittance must be reported on the withholding tax return before the fund leaves China. Failure to report an outbound distribution will trigger separate penalties, interest, and blacklisting exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL): the tax authority orders correction within a fixed time and imposes a fine up to RMB 2,000, or between RMB 2,000 and RMB 10,000 in serious circumstances. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the statutory due date. Under TCAL Article 63, conduct constituting tax evasion, such as false related-party invoices or deliberately understated income, results in recovery of the underpaid tax plus a monetary penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid amount. A withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit outbound tax is exposed under TCAL Article 69 to a fine of 50% to 3 times the unwithheld amount. Significant violations are published on the tax credit blacklist, trigger travel and exit restrictions for the legal representative, and can lead to criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to 7 years for especially large underpayments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid to a non-resident enterprise under EIT Law Article 37 and Article 3 of the implementation regulations. Under the China-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement, the rate is reduced to 5% where the Hong Kong shareholder is the beneficial owner and directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's paid-in capital; because the WFOE is a 100% subsidiary, the 5% treaty rate applies if beneficial ownership and substance are proven. If the beneficial owner is not established, the rate is 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the China-HK DTA reduced rate, the following mandatory procedural steps are required: (i) the Hong Kong shareholder must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department evidencing central management and control in Hong Kong; (ii) the WFOE must complete the withholding tax filing through the electronic tax portal and declare the specific DTA article on which relief is based; (iii) the WFOE must file a non-resident enterprise beneficial owner self-assessment with supporting board resolutions, invoices or contracts, bank settlement records, and proof that the Hong Kong shareholder is not a conduit; (iv) the taxpayer must satisfy the economic substance conditions set out in SAT Announcement 2018 No.9, including presence, personnel, decision-making, and risk-management functions in Hong Kong; (v) the WFOE must retain the TRC, the tax payment certificate, the withholding return, and all underlying ownership and substance documentation for at least 10 years; and (vi) if the Hong Kong shareholder or WFOE structure has been inserted primarily to obtain the benefit, the Principal Purpose Test in the Multilateral Instrument will deny relief and the rate reverts to 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest paid to a non-resident enterprise is 10%; under the China-HK DTA the treaty rate is 7% for a Hong Kong resident beneficial owner. Statutory withholding tax on royalties is 10%; under the China-HK DTA the treaty rate is 5% for qualifying copyright, patent, trademark, know-how, and certain industrial or commercial royalties where the Hong Kong resident is the beneficial owner. A factoring discount is normally recharacterized as interest because the legal substance is a debt-financing arrangement, so the relevant treaty rate is 7%, not 5%. If the contract bundles factoring software access or proprietary trade-finance processes with the discount, the fee may be split and the royalty portion treated at the 5% treaty rate, provided the royalty has been separately priced and is beneficially owned by the Hong Kong resident. All outbound interest and royalty payments require gross-basis withholding, supporting DTA claim forms, TRC, and beneficial ownership documentation; gross-ups are not automatically permitted and must be contractually
